Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant. An oriented link is a finite
disjoint union of oriented smooth circles embedded in $S^3$, considered up to
ambient isotopy; an oriented classical knot is the one-component case. For a nonempty
oriented link $L\subset S^3$, let $V_L(x)\in\mathbb Z[x^{\pm1}]$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$;
write $V_K$ for its value on a knot $K$. Here $x=t^{1/2}$ in the library
convention $t=A^{-4}$, so an oriented skein triple satisfies
$$x^{-2}V_{L_+}(x)-x^2V_{L_-}(x)=(x-x^{-1})V_{L_0}(x).$$
Set $p=x-x^{-1}$. By the unique Laurent decomposition, write
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where $a_q(K),b_q(K)\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. The
**Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vector of order $q$** is
$$f_q(K):=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T},$$
and $c_q(K):=a_q(K)+b_q(K)$. This is the algebraic coefficient-vector
definition used by Carmi and Cohen. The claim that the coordinates of $f_q$
are finite-type invariants of order at most $q$ is a separate theorem and is
not part of this definition.

consumers.public_clause_literal: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. consumers.public_clause_literal: Fix either a strict Morse knot presentation $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ or a compact strict Morse tangle $T\subset\mathbb C\times[a,b]$ with distinct regular boundary points, and a degree $m\ge0$. Each degree-$m$ coefficient of the unframed Kontsevich series is an absolutely convergent improper integral after summing its finitely many pairing terms in the 4T+1T quotient. A critical needle of width $\varepsilon$ in a horizontal slab is a local arc $N_\varepsilon$ whose intersection with each horizontal disk in the slab has at most two points and whose horizontal diameter is at most $\varepsilon$, with the knot or tangle fixed outside the slab and with the nondegenerate critical-point charts uniformly bounded in a compact smooth family. For every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals that have at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, where $C_m$ is independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero as the needle narrows.

Let $T_1\subset\mathbb C\times[a,c]$ and $T_2\subset\mathbb C\times[c,b]$ be compact strict Morse tangles whose boundary points and orientations match at the regular level $c$, with the joined tangle $T=T_2\circ T_1$ smooth and embedded. Their unframed configuration integrals converge absolutely degreewise and satisfy
$$
Z(T_2\circ T_1)=Z(T_2)\,Z(T_1),
$$
where multiplication stacks tangle diagrams with $T_2$ above $T_1$. The equality holds in the completed unframed tangle diagram space and uses only the finite-degree integrals defined on the matched pieces.

consumers.public_clause_literal:
Let $T$ be a compact strict Morse tangle in $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$ whose skeleton is one oriented arc with exactly one boundary point on each boundary plane, oriented from the lower point to the upper point. For sufficiently large $R$, close $T$ to an embedded oriented circle $K_R$ by adding a lower cap with one nondegenerate minimum, an upper cap with one nondegenerate maximum, and a return arc that is vertical at horizontal coordinate $R$ over $[a,b]$. Choose the smooth joins in regular height collars so that varying $R$ moves only regular arcs and fixes both cap critical neighborhoods. Let $\operatorname{cl}$ be the linear map that closes an interval chord diagram on $T$ to a circle chord diagram by joining its two boundary ends along the outside closure arc. For closed chord diagrams, let $\#$ be connected-sum multiplication, formed by concatenating diagrams at the closure cut. For oriented knot closures, connected sum is formed by deleting a short arc from each knot and joining the four ends in the orientation-preserving order outside their compact tangles. Then
$$
Z(K_R)=\operatorname{cl}(Z(T)),
$$
independently of the sufficiently large choice of $R$. If $T_1,T_2$ each have one-arc skeletons and are compact strict Morse one-in one-out tangles whose vertical composite is smooth and embedded, then the closure of $T_2\circ T_1$ is the connected sum of their closures and
$$
Z(\operatorname{cl}(T_2\circ T_1))=Z(\operatorname{cl}(T_2))\# Z(\operatorname{cl}(T_1)).
$$
The figure is schematic: height increases upward, arrows give the orientation, the lower and upper caps have one minimum and one maximum, and the return arc is the vertical branch at $R$. The second panel shows the oriented seam used for vertical stacking and closure; neither panel is used as a proof.

consumers.public_clause_literal:
For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

consumers.public_clause_literal: Let $K_0,K_1$ be strict Morse presentations of smooth oriented knots. Define a horizontal deformation to be a smooth family $K_s(x)=(z_s(x),t(x))$ that fixes neighborhoods of all height critical points. Define a critical-point move to be a smooth family fixed outside one local arc containing a single nondegenerate critical point in a horizontal slab, such that horizontal deformations can narrow the moving arc to every sufficiently small width $\varepsilon$, each horizontal disk meets that arc in at most two points, and its Morse charts remain uniformly bounded. Let a standard hump birth or death mean insertion or deletion of the fixed local maximum-minimum pair used in the normalization.

consumers.public_clause_literal: For $q\ge0$, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the degreewise completion of the algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ for four distinct indices and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ for distinct $i,j,k$. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a chord joining strands $i,j$. Set $\Omega_q=(2\pi i)^{-1}\sum_{i<j}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$; tangential endpoint transport removes the local residue factors. For $1\le i\le q$, let $\epsilon_i:\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)\to\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q-1)$ delete strand $i$ and kill any diagram with a chord endpoint on it. Let $\Delta_i:\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)\to\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q+1)$ double strand $i$ into adjacent parallel copies and sum over all assignments of its chord endpoints to either copy. For $\Phi$ on three strands, let $\Phi_{ijk}$ relabel strands $1,2,3$ as $i,j,k$; $\Phi\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathrm{id}\otimes\Phi$ place the associator on the indicated three adjacent strands. Products stack from bottom to top, so the rightmost factor acts first. Put $R_{ij}:=\exp(t_{ij}/2)$.

consumers.public_clause_literal:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be an $n$-singular oriented knot with $n\ge0$ transverse double points and chord diagram $D\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$. Choose disjoint crossing balls and a common height presentation so that the two branches at every singular point are monotone in height inside their ball, all $2^n$ resolutions are strict Morse, and their height functions and number $r$ of local maxima agree outside the crossing balls. Define
$$
\Delta^n I(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^n\epsilon_i\right)I(K_\epsilon).
$$
Then $\Delta^n I(K)$ has zero homogeneous components in degrees $m<n$, its degree-$n$ component is exactly $D$, and all remaining terms have degree greater than $n$. For $n=0$, the degree-zero component is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$. The conclusion is in the unframed 4T+1T chord-diagram completion and makes no rational-coefficient claim.

consumers.public_clause_literal: Assume countable choice, and let $I_m(K)$ be the degree-$m$ homogeneous coefficient of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series $I(K)$ of a smooth oriented knot type $K$. For $n\ge0$, put $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}I_m(K)$. A function on knot types is of type at most $n$ when its alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero. Then $I_{\le n}$ is a type-at-most-$n$ invariant with values in the complexified direct sum $\bigoplus_{m=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_m^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ of the rational unframed degree-$m$ chord-diagram modules. For every $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, its $n$-fold finite difference satisfies $D_n I_{\le n}(K)=D$. In particular, the degree-$n$ symbol is the identity on rational chord diagrams after extending scalars to $\mathbb C$; no rational-coefficient claim is made about $I_m(K)$.

consumers.public_clause_literal:
Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ be the $\mathbb C$-vector space of ambient-isotopy invariants of oriented knots with values in $\mathbb C$ and type at most $n$, where type at most $n$ means that the alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero; set $\mathcal V_{-1}^{\mathbb C}=0$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be the rational vector space on degree-$n$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T; a weight system is a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on this space. For an $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, define $\sigma_n([V])(D)$ to be the $n$-fold alternating resolution sum of $V$ on that knot. Let $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}I_j(K)$ be the degree-$n$ truncation of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series. The degree-$n$ symbol map
$$
\sigma_n:\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}/\mathcal V_{n-1}^{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}},\mathbb C)
$$
is surjective. In particular, every rational weight system has a complex-valued finite-type lift; no rationality claim is made about that lift or about the coefficients of $I(K)$. Moreover, for every $n$ and every $V\in\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ there is a complex-linear functional $\Lambda_V$ on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ whose degree-$n$ restriction is the degree-$n$ symbol of $V$ and such that
$$
V(K)=\Lambda_V(I_{\le n}(K))
$$
for every oriented knot type $K$. This recovery statement does not imply that distinct knot types have distinct Kontsevich series.
